title: needs-decision: per-PR terminal tail under an active outage declaration
body:
## Background

Even with every roadmap `#2318` track landed, a pull request advancing
under an active outage relief declaration must still earn its own
terminal advisory-unavailable state on its final HEAD:
`advisoryWait.recoveryCycleCap` (default 2) completed recovery cycles,
then `advisoryWait.terminalWindow` (default 12 h) measured from the
GitHub `created_at` of the earliest bound current-HEAD
`advisory-recovery` marker. Both are current-HEAD-scoped, so each
review-fix push restarts them.

The declaration (`#2320`) deliberately removes only the
per-pull-request waiver-authoring cost; it never bypasses the
per-pull-request terminal state. The arithmetic that remains: every
merge during a declared outage carries a tail of roughly the recovery
cycle time plus 12 hours after that pull request's final push. During
a multi-week outage with active CodeRabbit/Codex review rounds — whose
fix pushes restart the clocks — sustained throughput is capped by that
tail per pull request.

## Question

Is that tail the intended posture (fail-closed, bounded, slow), or
should policy allow tuning it while a valid declaration is active?

Options, for the record:

- **Accept as designed.** Document the expected tail; no mechanism
  changes. Cheapest, and keeps `#1572`'s non-bypass property untouched.
- **Declaration-scoped window override.** A `providerOutage`-scoped
  terminal-window value that applies only while a valid declaration is
  active. A bounded loosening of a merge-gate input; needs the same
  fail-closed review as the declaration itself.
- **Credit the declaration's age.** Count validated repository-wide
  outage duration toward each pull request's window. Changes evidence
  semantics from per-HEAD observation to shared state; the most
  invasive option.

## Why this is not execution-ready

Any option other than the first widens how quickly a required-check
relief can be reached, touching the same non-bypass property `#1572`
protects. That is a policy choice for the repository owner, not a
mechanical fix, so this issue carries `status:needs-decision` and stays
below the autopilot floor until the choice is recorded.

Refs roadmap `#2318`; context: `#2320`, `#2327`, pull request `#2325`.
